profile_text.body:
The Algorithmic Justice League is a nonprofit founded in 2016 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its site describes its mission as raising awareness about the impacts of AI, equipping advocates with empirical research, building the voice and choice of the most impacted communities, and galvanizing researchers, policy makers, and industry practitioners to mitigate AI harms and biases. The organization says AI systems are used to decide who gets hired, the quality of medical treatment people receive, and whether someone becomes a suspect in a police investigation, and that such systems can amplify racism, sexism, ableism, and other forms of discrimination.

Its site highlights a campaign on facial recognition in airports, noting that the TSA is expanding its use of the technology and that travelers can opt out, and it asks people to share their experiences with airport face scans. It also points to the film Coded Bias, which it says shows how the organization began, tells the stories of people impacted by harmful technology, and features women raising alarms about threats AI poses to civil rights. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020. The site asks supporters to become monthly sustainers.

No AI products are attributed to the organization, and no lawsuits or MCP servers are listed for it. A Massachusetts law exposure count of 126 is recorded.
